messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Maladaptive Strategies
  - Memory
  - Negative Appraisals
  - Triggers

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Triggers → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Triggers → Memory
  - Triggers → Negative Appraisals
  - Negative Appraisals → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Negative Appraisals → Memory
  - Negative Appraisals → Triggers
  - Memory → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Memory → Negative Appraisals
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Negative Appraisals
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Triggers

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

Ryan's eyes scanned the empty halls of his school, a familiar sense of dread settling in as he caught a whiff of disinfectant. It was a smell that transported him back to the hospital, where just over a year ago, he had spent weeks fighting for his life against a relentless illness. The scent was overpowering, and Ryan's mind began to reel as memories long suppressed threatened to surface. He knew what would happen if he let those memories take hold – the same debilitating anxiety that had taken over his life since the hospital stay would kick in, rendering him unable to function. So, he did what he always did: rehearsed conversations with staff members, mentally preparing himself for every possible scenario, a desperate attempt to regain control. He also avoided going near the school nurse's office, fearing any reminders of medical procedures might trigger another episode. The irony wasn't lost on Ryan – as a principal, he was expected to be a pillar of strength, yet his own body had betrayed him in ways he couldn't shake off. Some days, it felt like his memories were fragmented and inaccessible, while others brought the full emotional intensity without any clear image or recollection. There were moments when his body would involuntarily contort into the same position as during those harrowing hospital days, sending him spiraling back. The hardest part for Ryan was recognizing himself in this new reality – he had become unrecognizable to himself, unable to rely on his own judgment or trust his body. His entire identity was now intertwined with feelings of inadequacy and self-doubt. When these thoughts consumed him, Ryan cut off contact with friends and family, further isolating himself from the world. The vicious cycle fed itself – Ryan's desperate attempts to regain control by rehearsing conversations only led to increased anxiety when he inevitably failed to predict every outcome. His memories, fragmented and painful as they were, reinforced his conviction that he couldn't trust himself or his body. This distrust fueled more avoidance behaviors, particularly around medical settings. Recently, Ryan had caught a glimpse of an ambulance outside the school – its sirens silent but menacing – and something inside him snapped. He realized he needed help breaking free from this self-perpetuating nightmare, even if it meant confronting those unbearable memories head-on. The hardest part would be admitting to others that he, the once-strong principal, was no longer in control of his own life. As Ryan navigated these treacherous waters, a glimmer of hope flickered – maybe with help, he could find a way to reconcile this shattered self and rebuild trust in himself and his body.
